## WhatsApp check

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/miscale-news/whatsapp-check.md

Description: Check whether a phone number is registered on WhatsApp and reconcile uncertain operations.

Check whether a mobile number is registered on WhatsApp. The check returns a durable operation ID so clients can reconcile a request when a provider response is delayed or lost.

## Contract summary

<Badge color="blue">POST</Badge> `/v1/whatsapp-check`

<Badge color="green">GET</Badge> `/v1/whatsapp-check/operations/{operation_id}`

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Authentication | Bearer Airscale API key |
| Request body | Exactly one `phone` field |
| Phone format | Strict E.164: `+` followed by 7–15 digits |
| Rate limit | 60 requests per minute per workspace |
| Credit cost | 1 credit for a definitive result |
| Execution | Synchronous check with durable reconciliation |

## Check a phone number

Send exactly one phone field. Do not include spaces, punctuation, or additional fields.

```json
{
  "phone": "+14155550123"
}
```

An `Idempotency-Key` header is optional. When supplied, it must be a UUID generated by your application. Reuse the same key and request body when retrying a request whose response was lost or timed out.

```bash cURL
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.airscale.io/v1/whatsapp-check \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $AIRSCALE_API_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --header "Idempotency-Key: 5f73072e-1bb5-4f58-845b-4e65e86b74d4" \
  --data '{"phone":"+14155550123"}'
```

```python Python
import os
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.airscale.io/v1/whatsapp-check",
    headers={
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['AIRSCALE_API_KEY']}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Idempotency-Key": "5f73072e-1bb5-4f58-845b-4e65e86b74d4",
    },
    json={"phone": "+14155550123"},
    timeout=30,
)
response.raise_for_status()
print(response.json())
```

```javascript Node.js
const apiKey = process.env.AIRSCALE_API_KEY;
const response = await fetch("https://api.airscale.io/v1/whatsapp-check", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID(),
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ phone: "+14155550123" }),
});

if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`WhatsApp check failed: ${response.status}`);
console.log(await response.json());
```

## Check response

A definitive `200 OK` response includes the operation ID, normalized phone number, WhatsApp result, and one consumed credit.

```json
{
  "operation_id": "5f73072e-1bb5-4f58-845b-4e65e86b74d4",
  "phone": "+14155550123",
  "whatsapp": "yes",
  "credits_consumed": 1
}
```

`whatsapp` is either `yes` or `no`. An unavailable result returns `503` and consumes no credit. When the request cannot be completed definitively, the response includes an `operation_id` and a `202` state that you can reconcile.

## Reconcile an operation

Use the operation ID returned by the check. The lookup must use an API key from the same workspace.

```bash cURL
curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.airscale.io/v1/whatsapp-check/operations/5f73072e-1bb5-4f58-845b-4e65e86b74d4 \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $AIRSCALE_API_KEY"
```

While processing, the lookup can return:

```json
{
  "operation_id": "5f73072e-1bb5-4f58-845b-4e65e86b74d4",
  "status": "pending"
}
```

The lookup returns a terminal response when the operation is complete:

```json
{
  "operation_id": "5f73072e-1bb5-4f58-845b-4e65e86b74d4",
  "status": "completed",
  "whatsapp": "no",
  "credits_consumed": 1
}
```

`unknown` is also a `202` state and should be reconciled before retrying. A request made without an idempotency key can create a new paid operation if the original response was lost. Use and reuse your own UUID key when retry protection is required.

## Errors

| Status | Meaning | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid JSON, phone format, operation ID, or idempotency key. | Send exactly one strict E.164 `phone` field and valid UUID values. |
| `401 Unauthorized` | The API key is missing or invalid. | Send a valid workspace API key. |
| `403 Forbidden` | The workspace does not have enough credits. | Add credits before retrying. |
| `404 Not Found` | The operation does not exist in the workspace. | Check the operation ID and workspace key. |
| `409 Conflict` | An idempotency key was reused with different input. | Use the original request body or a new UUID. |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | The workspace exceeded 60 requests in one minute. | Retry after the rate-limit window. |
| `503 Service Unavailable` | The check or its durable operation store is unavailable. | Reconcile the operation ID before retrying. |

---

## Meta Ads

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/miscale-news/meta-ads.md

Description: Check whether a domain has active Meta ads.

Check whether a company domain has active Meta ads. Airscale normalizes a bare host or an HTTP(S) URL before running the lookup.

## Contract summary

<Badge color="blue">POST</Badge> `/v1/meta-ads`

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Authentication | Bearer Airscale API key |
| Request body | Exactly one `domain` field |
| Rate limit | 60 requests per minute per workspace |
| Credit cost | 1 credit for a positive ad count; 0 credits for zero or non-billable results |
| Execution | Synchronous |

## Request

The body must contain exactly one `domain` field. Use a bare hostname or an HTTP(S) URL. Paths are ignored after the host is normalized.

```json
{
  "domain": "airscale.io"
}
```

```bash cURL
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.airscale.io/v1/meta-ads \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $AIRSCALE_API_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"domain":"airscale.io"}'
```

```python Python
import os
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.airscale.io/v1/meta-ads",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['AIRSCALE_API_KEY']}"},
    json={"domain": "airscale.io"},
    timeout=30,
)
response.raise_for_status()
print(response.json())
```

```javascript Node.js
const apiKey = process.env.AIRSCALE_API_KEY;
const response = await fetch("https://api.airscale.io/v1/meta-ads", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ domain: "airscale.io" }),
});

if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Meta Ads lookup failed: ${response.status}`);
console.log(await response.json());
```

## Response

A positive finite `number_of_ads` consumes one credit.

```json
{
  "page_id": "meta-123",
  "number_of_ads": 4,
  "credits_consumed": 1
}
```

A zero, missing, non-numeric, or non-positive ad count consumes no credit.

```json
{
  "page_id": "meta-zero",
  "number_of_ads": 0,
  "credits_consumed": 0
}
```

The endpoint does not support an idempotency key. A retry can run another provider lookup.

## Errors

| Status | Meaning | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid JSON, extra fields, unsupported URL, or unsafe domain. | Send exactly one public hostname or HTTP(S) URL in `domain`. |
| `401 Unauthorized` | The API key is missing or invalid. | Send a valid workspace API key. |
| `403 Forbidden` | The workspace does not have enough credits for a possible positive result. | Add credits before retrying. |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | The workspace exceeded 60 requests in one minute. | Retry after the rate-limit window. |
| `502 Bad Gateway` | The upstream Meta Ads lookup failed. | Retry with bounded backoff. |
| `503 Service Unavailable` | Authentication, rate limiting, configuration, or settlement is unavailable. | Retry after the service recovers. |

---

## Email verifier

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/miscale-news/email-verifier.md

Description: Verify the deliverability of one email address.

Verify one email address through Airscale's deliverability service. The versioned route is the documented API path. The legacy `/email-verifier` path remains available as a compatibility alias.

## Contract summary

<Badge color="blue">POST</Badge> `/v1/email-verifier`

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Authentication | Bearer Airscale API key |
| Request body | Exactly one `email` field |
| Credit cost | 0.5 credits per valid verification request |
| Execution | Synchronous; may poll the provider for up to 45 seconds |
| Rate limit | No endpoint throttle |

## Request

The body must contain exactly one valid `email` field. The endpoint rejects extra fields, empty values, invalid email syntax, and bodies larger than 16 KiB.

```json
{
  "email": "maya@example.com"
}
```

```bash cURL
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.airscale.io/v1/email-verifier \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $AIRSCALE_API_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"email":"maya@example.com"}'
```

```python Python
import os
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.airscale.io/v1/email-verifier",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['AIRSCALE_API_KEY']}"},
    json={"email": "maya@example.com"},
    timeout=90,
)
response.raise_for_status()
print(response.json())
```

```javascript Node.js
const apiKey = process.env.AIRSCALE_API_KEY;
const response = await fetch("https://api.airscale.io/v1/email-verifier", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ email: "maya@example.com" }),
  signal: AbortSignal.timeout(90_000),
});

if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Email verification failed: ${response.status}`);
console.log(await response.json());
```

## Response

A terminal response reports the provider result and `credits_consumed: 0.5`. The provider may return additional fields, which Airscale preserves in the response body.

```json
{
  "email": "maya@example.com",
  "result": "deliverable",
  "credits_consumed": 0.5
}
```

When the provider initially reports `verifying`, Airscale polls the provider's status endpoint without repeating the paid request or charging a second time. If the provider does not reach a terminal result within the polling window, Airscale returns a successful response with `result: "risky"`.

If the initial provider request returns a non-2xx response, Airscale refunds the reserved credits when possible and passes through the provider status and response body. Provider failure can therefore return the provider's status, such as `422`, rather than a normalized `200` response.

## Errors

| Status | Meaning | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid JSON or email body. | Send exactly one valid `email` field. |
| `401 Unauthorized` | The API key is missing or invalid. | Send a valid workspace API key. |
| `403 Forbidden` | The workspace does not have 0.5 credits available. | Add credits before retrying. |
| `413 Content Too Large` | The request body exceeds 16 KiB. | Send a smaller JSON body. |
| `422 Unprocessable Content` | The provider rejected the verification request and its response was passed through. | Correct the request if indicated and retry. |
| `500 Internal Server Error` | Email verifier provider configuration is unavailable. | Retry after configuration is restored. |
| `502 Bad Gateway` | The provider could not be reached. | Retry with bounded backoff. |
| `503 Service Unavailable` | Authentication, credit settlement, or provider recovery is unavailable. | Retry after the service recovers. |

---

## Create a job-change monitor

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/job-change-monitors/create.md

Description: Start monitoring personal LinkedIn profiles for employer changes.

Create an active monitor for one to 500 personal LinkedIn profiles with [Bearer authentication](/api-reference/authentication). Each successful request creates a new monitor. If a network failure leaves the result unknown, list or retrieve monitors before retrying so you do not create an unintended duplicate.

<Note>
The `frequency` can be `weekly`, `every_30_days`, or `every_90_days`. If you provide `webhook_url`, store the returned `signing_secret` immediately; it is returned only on the first successful create response.
</Note>

Airschool canonicalizes LinkedIn URLs and preserves each profile's optional `external_id` in later events. Monitoring admission checks the workspace's configured provider, capacity, and credit balance before accepting the monitor.

## Verify webhook signatures

Airscale sends `job_change.detected` as a JSON `POST` to `webhook_url`. The request includes `X-Airscale-Event-Id`, `X-Airscale-Timestamp`, and `X-Airscale-Signature: sha256=<hex>`. Compute HMAC-SHA256 with the one-time `signing_secret` over `<timestamp>.<raw request body>`, compare it in constant time, and reject timestamps older than five minutes. Return a 2xx response only after durable handling. Retries keep the same event ID and are deduplicated by Airscale internally.

## Next step

Use [List job-change monitors](/api-reference/job-change-monitors/list) to confirm the monitor's status and next check time.

---

## List job-change monitors

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/job-change-monitors/list.md

Description: List the monitors and unread-event counts in a workspace.

List every job-change monitor in the authenticated workspace. Each monitor includes its current status, schedule, active profile count, and unread event count.

<Info>
This operation is read-only and does not change schedules or consume monitoring credits.
</Info>

Use the monitor `id` returned here with the detail, update, profile, and event operations. A paused monitor remains in the list so you can resume it later.

## Next step

Open [Get a monitor](/api-reference/job-change-monitors/get) for its profiles and latest events.

---

## Get a job-change monitor

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/job-change-monitors/get.md

Description: Retrieve one monitor, its profiles, and its latest events.

Retrieve one monitor by `monitor_id`. The response contains all profiles, including soft-removed profiles, and up to the latest 200 events ordered newest first.

<Note>
Use the profile `status` and `removed_at` fields to distinguish an active profile from one removed from future checks. Historical events remain available after a profile is removed.
</Note>

The monitor object reports `next_check_at` and `last_successful_check_at` as ISO 8601 timestamps. A paused monitor has no next check scheduled.

## Next step

Use [List job-change events](/api-reference/job-change-monitors/events) when you need cursor pagination beyond the latest 200 events.

## Update a job-change monitor

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/job-change-monitors/update.md

Description: Change a monitor's name or frequency, or pause and resume checks.

Update one or more monitor fields with `PATCH`. Send a new `name`, a supported `frequency`, an `action` of `pause`, or an `action` of `resume`.

<Warning>
Resuming requires at least one active profile and reruns monitoring admission. Changing the frequency updates the next check when the monitor is resumed; pausing clears the scheduled check.
</Warning>

The response returns the complete updated monitor, including its active profile and unread event counts.

## Next step

Use [Add profiles](/api-reference/job-change-monitors/profiles/add) before resuming a monitor with no active profiles.

---

## Delete a job-change monitor

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/job-change-monitors/delete.md

Description: Permanently remove a monitor and its stored monitoring data.

Delete a monitor by `monitor_id`. This permanently removes the monitor, its profile baselines, and its events from the workspace.

<Warning>
Deletion cannot be undone. Remove individual profiles instead when you need to stop checking a contact while retaining its event history.
</Warning>

The operation returns `{ "ok": true }` after the monitor and its cascaded data are deleted.

## Next step

Use [List job-change monitors](/api-reference/job-change-monitors/list) to verify the monitor no longer appears.

---

## Add profiles to a job-change monitor

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/job-change-monitors/profiles/add.md

Description: Add personal LinkedIn profiles while preserving existing baselines.

Add one to 500 personal LinkedIn profiles to an existing monitor. Airschool ignores a URL that is already active and reports how many profiles were actually added.

<Note>
Adding a URL after it was removed creates a new profile and a new baseline. The previous profile's events remain associated with its original profile ID.
</Note>

The response includes the newly created profile records, `added_profile_count`, and the monitor's resulting `active_profile_count`. The 500-profile limit applies to the monitor's active profiles.

## Next step

Use [Get a monitor](/api-reference/job-change-monitors/get) to inspect each profile's baseline and scan status.

---

## Remove a profile from a job-change monitor

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/job-change-monitors/profiles/remove.md

Description: Stop checking one profile while preserving its event history.

Soft-remove one profile with its `monitor_id` and `profile_id`. The profile no longer participates in future checks, but its record and event history remain available.

<Info>
To monitor the same LinkedIn URL again, call [Add profiles](/api-reference/job-change-monitors/profiles/add). Airschool creates a new profile ID and baseline instead of reusing the removed history.
</Info>

The returned profile has `status: "removed"` and a `removed_at` timestamp. Removing a profile does not pause the monitor or affect its other active profiles.

## Next step

Use [List job-change events](/api-reference/job-change-monitors/events) to review the retained history.

---

## List job-change events

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/job-change-monitors/events.md

Description: Read cursor-paginated employer-change events for a monitor.

List job-change events for one monitor, newest first. Set `limit` from 1 to 100; when `next_cursor` is not `null`, send that value unchanged as `cursor` on the next request.

<Note>
An event is created when a checked profile's employer identity changes. The event includes your `external_id` when one was supplied for the profile.
</Note>

Events include the previous and new employer identities, detection time, and `read_at`. This endpoint is also the durable fallback when webhook delivery is delayed or unavailable.

## Next step

Use [Mark an event as read](/api-reference/job-change-monitors/events/read) after your application has processed an event.

---

## Mark a job-change event as read

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/job-change-monitors/events/read.md

Description: Acknowledge one job-change event after processing it.

Mark one event as read after your integration has handled it. The response returns the event with its `read_at` timestamp, and the monitor's unread count decreases.

<Info>
Treat the event ID as the durable acknowledgement key. Webhook retries use the same event ID, so processing it idempotently prevents duplicate downstream work.
</Info>

Reading an event does not delete it. You can still retrieve it through [List job-change events](/api-reference/job-change-monitors/events) or the monitor detail response.

## Next step

Review [Create a job-change monitor](/api-reference/job-change-monitors/create) for webhook setup and one-time signing-secret handling.

---

## Credit count

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/api-reference/credit-count.md

Description: Check the remaining credit balance for your Airschool workspace.

Read the remaining credit balance for the workspace associated with your API key before starting paid enrichment work.

<Note>
Send no request body. Checking the balance is free and does not debit Airschool credits.
</Note>

An invalid or missing key returns `401 Unauthorized`. Confirm the current key in the Airschool dashboard and update your server-side secret; rotate it only if it was exposed.

## Next step

Use your authenticated client to [find people](/api-reference/find-people), or review [Authentication](/api-reference/authentication) before sending requests.

---

## How to use the Airschool MCP (+Claude demo)

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/mcp/how-to-use-the-airscale-mcp.md

Description: Prospect through conversation with Airschool search, enrichment, and export tools.

Prospect without leaving your AI chat. Airschool connects Claude, ChatGPT, and other compatible assistants to search, enrichment, research, and export tools, so you can build a list through natural-language conversation.

<Frame>
  <iframe
    className="w-full aspect-video rounded-xl"
    src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/t4coJ0P8YVM"
    title="How to prospect with Airschool MCP in Claude"
    allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share"
    referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
    allowFullScreen
  />
</Frame>

## What is the Airschool MCP?

The Airschool MCP gives your assistant 22 typed tools that can:

- Check your workspace credit balance.
- Search for people and companies.
- Discover valid Find Companies filters before searching.
- Enrich contact details and person or company profiles.
- Run Airsearch for structured web research.
- Create downloadable CSV or JSONL exports.

See the [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools) for every tool and its inputs.

## How credits work

Find People costs 0.1 credit per returned person. Find Companies costs 0.1 credit per returned company. Airsearch costs 2 credits per call.

Credit checks, people counts, and Find Companies filter discovery are free planning tools. Other enrichment follows linked API pricing in the related references for [contact data](/api-reference/email-finder), [people profiles](/api-reference/extract-people-profile), and [company profiles](/api-reference/extract-company-profile).

Before a paid export starts, review the final filters, row limit, and maximum spend, then explicitly confirm that paid action. No paid search, enrichment, or export should run before your approval.

## Run a search in natural language

Describe the cohort and keep the first result small. The example prompts below are illustrative and non-executing; they instruct your assistant to pause before every paid action.

> Find up to five cybersecurity companies in France with 51–200 employees. Before you run it, show me the proposed tool, filters, row limit, and maximum cost, then wait for my approval.

Your assistant can use a free filter-discovery tool first when a value needs validation. Approve only the bounded search you reviewed.

### Review your results

Review the company name, domain, website, country, and filter precision before expanding the search. At 0.1 credit per returned company, a five-company sample costs at most 0.5 credits.

### Enrich contacts through conversation

Begin with a bounded role-discovery request for only the companies you approved:

> Discovery step: For the approved companies, discover at most one CEO, one CFO, and one Head of Growth per approved company. Show me the proposed tool, per-step maximum cost, and cumulative workflow maximum, then wait for my approval.

Review the discovered people and approve the decision-makers you want to continue with. Then request only their professional work emails:

> Professional work email enrichment step: For only the approved decision-makers, find professional work emails. Show me the proposed tool, contact count, per-step maximum cost, and new cumulative workflow maximum, then wait for my approval.

Review the requested fields and linked pricing before approving each stage. Keep each follow-up bounded, and do not add unapproved companies or contacts to the request.

## Export your final list

People and company exports perform a fresh paid search from the final filters. They do not export the selected chat rows, may return different rows, and add a new charge in addition to earlier paid steps in the workflow.

Before starting, require the assistant to repeat the exact filters, fields, format, `max_rows`, additional maximum credits, and cumulative workflow maximum, then wait for your approval.

Exports are asynchronous: start one export, check its status, then retrieve the file after completion. Save the returned `export_id` and reuse the same `export_id` for status and file requests.

Do not start a duplicate export while the existing job is `queued` or `running`; follow the returned `poll_after_seconds` interval instead. When status is `completed` or `failed`, stop polling; retrieve the file only after completion.

## Get started

- [Connect Airschool MCP to ChatGPT](/mcp/connect-airscale-mcp-to-chatgpt)
- [Connect Airschool MCP to Claude](/mcp/connect-airscale-mcp-to-claude)
- [Read the Airschool MCP server reference](/mcp/airscale-mcp-server)

---

## Connect Airschool MCP to ChatGPT

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/mcp/connect-airscale-mcp-to-chatgpt.md

Description: Connect ChatGPT to Airschool through browser OAuth and validate the connection without spending credits.

Connect ChatGPT to your Airschool workspace with browser OAuth, then verify the connection with a free tool call before you approve any paid work.

## MCP server URL

Use the official remote MCP endpoint exactly as shown:

```text
https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp
```

## What ChatGPT can do with Airschool MCP

Airschool MCP gives ChatGPT 22 typed tools that can:

- Check the authorized workspace's credit balance.
- Search for people and companies.
- Count matches and discover accepted filter values before a paid search.
- Enrich work contact details and extract people or company profiles.
- Run Airsearch web research.
- Create downloadable people or company exports.

Managed large contact enrichment is work-email-only in its current phase. Review exact inputs and credit behavior in the [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools).

## Before you start

You need an Airschool account with access to the intended workspace, API access enabled, and an active workspace credential. You also need a ChatGPT account and workspace where Developer mode is available; availability can depend on account and workspace policy.

ChatGPT uses browser OAuth for this connection: if prompted, the browser asks you to sign in to Airschool, choose a workspace, and authorize ChatGPT. OpenAI's [current plugin connection guide](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/connect-chatgpt) is the source for the navigation below.

After OAuth, Airschool's MCP server resolves the authorized workspace's current credential server-side on each tool call; ChatGPT neither receives nor stores that API key. Do not paste an Airschool API key into ChatGPT, prompts, or tool inputs.

## Step-by-step setup

<Steps>
  <Step title="Enable Developer mode">
    Open **Settings → Security and login**, then turn on **Developer mode**. Developer mode availability can depend on account and workspace policy.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open ChatGPT Plugins">
    Go to **ChatGPT Plugins** and select the plus button.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Describe the connection">
    Enter a user-facing name and description, such as **Airschool MCP** and a short description of its search, enrichment, research, and export tools.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Connect and authorize Airschool">
    Under **Connection**, choose the public endpoint option and enter `https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp`, including the `/mcp` path. Create the connection. If prompted, complete browser OAuth, sign in to Airschool, select the intended workspace, and return to ChatGPT. Do not enter an API key or static authorization value.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Review discovered tools">
    Review the tools and metadata discovered from the server. Confirm that the Airschool connection shows the expected 22 typed tools before testing it.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Verify the connection for free">
    Start a new conversation, add the Airschool MCP connection from the tools menu, and run `airscale_check_credits` without another tool. A returned balance confirms tool discovery and authentication to an Airschool workspace without debiting credits, but it does not identify which workspace. Separately verify the workspace shown during OAuth before paid actions.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Recommended first prompts

The identities and domains below are synthetic.

> Use `airscale_check_credits` to show my current Airschool credit balance. Do not call another tool.

This is the free connection test. A returned balance confirms tool discovery and authentication to an Airschool workspace without debiting credits. It does not identify which workspace; verify the workspace shown during OAuth before paid actions.

> Count people named Jordan Example who work at `northstar.example`. Do not run a paid search.

> Plan an Airschool search for up to five companies matching `sample-company.test`. Show the proposed Airschool tool, arguments, and maximum cost, then wait for my approval.

For a complete staged sequence, follow the [safe MCP workflow](/mcp/how-to-use-the-airscale-mcp).

## Export behavior in ChatGPT

A people or company export performs a fresh paid search from the final filters; it does not package the selected chat rows and may return different rows. Before approval, review the exact filters, fields, format, `max_rows`, additional maximum credits, and cumulative workflow maximum.

An export has one asynchronous lifecycle: start the export once, check its status, then retrieve the file when it is ready. Reuse the same `export_id` and honor the returned `poll_after_seconds`. Do not start a duplicate export while the original job is queued or running.

## Credits and confirmation

The credit check, people count, company filter-value discovery, export status, and export-file retrieval are free. Search and enrichment tools can consume credits; Airsearch costs 2 credits per call. Managed contact enrichment is work-email-only in its current phase.

Paid export starts fail closed until `confirm_credit_spend` is explicitly `true`. Review ChatGPT's proposed tool, arguments, row limit, and maximum cost before confirming. An export can support up to 10,000 rows, but use the smallest limit that serves the task.

## Refreshing tools

If Airschool tools or metadata are stale, open the connection in **ChatGPT Plugins**, select **Refresh**, confirm the advertised metadata changed, then start a new conversation and add the connection again from the tools menu.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Developer mode is not visible">
    Open **Settings → Security and login** and look for **Developer mode**. Availability can depend on account and workspace policy, so ask the workspace administrator to check policy if the control is unavailable.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="The connection cannot be created">
    Confirm the exact public endpoint, including the `/mcp` path. Complete Airschool browser authorization if prompted, return to ChatGPT, and review any connection or discovered-tool errors before retrying.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Authentication succeeds but a tool fails">
    Confirm that the selected Airschool workspace has API access, an active workspace credential, and enough credits for the proposed paid tool. Run `airscale_check_credits` before retrying.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="An export remains queued">
    Poll `airscale_get_export_status` with the same identifier and the returned `poll_after_seconds`. Do not create another paid job.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Security note

Authorize only the Airschool workspace you intend to use. Keep secrets out of chats and tool inputs, review every proposed paid action, and remove the Airschool MCP connection when it is no longer needed.

## Need help?

- Review the [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools) for exact schemas and credit behavior.
- Use the [safe MCP workflow](/mcp/how-to-use-the-airscale-mcp) before running a search or export.
- Read the [Airschool MCP server overview](/mcp/airscale-mcp-server) for authentication and security guidance.

## Connect Airschool MCP to Claude

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/mcp/connect-airscale-mcp-to-claude.md

Description: Connect Claude clients to Airschool with hosted OAuth or a protected Claude Code authorization header.

Connect Claude to your Airschool workspace through hosted remote OAuth where supported, or configure Claude Code with a protected environment-backed header.

## MCP server URL

Use the official remote MCP endpoint exactly as shown:

```text
https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp
```

## What Claude can do with Airschool MCP

Airschool MCP gives Claude 22 typed tools that can:

- Check the authorized workspace's credit balance.
- Search for people and companies.
- Count matches and discover accepted filter values before a paid search.
- Enrich work contact details and extract people or company profiles.
- Run Airsearch web research.
- Create downloadable people or company exports.

Managed large contact enrichment is work-email-only in its current phase. Review exact inputs and credit behavior in the [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools).

## Before you start

You need an Airschool account with access to the intended workspace, API access enabled, and an active workspace credential.

Claude web and desktop clients can use remote OAuth in the browser where supported by the Claude account and client. Each hosted user signs in to Airschool and authorizes a workspace.

Claude Code can instead use a protected authorization header sourced from an environment variable. Hosted OAuth and Claude Code header authentication are separate connection methods. Never put the credential in a prompt or MCP tool argument.

## Claude web setup

Use the hosted connector flow that matches your Claude account. If availability or labels differ, check Anthropic's current [remote custom connector guide](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp).

### Individual Claude accounts

Individual Free, Pro, or Max accounts can add a custom connector directly. A Free account is limited to one custom connector.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open connector settings">
    Sign in to Claude web or desktop and open **Customize → Connectors**. Use the current connectors or integrations settings if the label differs.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Add Airschool">
    Choose the control to add a custom connector, name it **Airschool MCP**, and enter `https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp` as the remote server URL.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Authorize your Airschool workspace">
    Continue to the browser sign-in, authenticate with Airschool, select the intended workspace, approve access, and return to Claude.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Enable the tools">
    Select Airschool MCP for a new conversation and confirm that Claude can see its tools.
  </Step>
</Steps>

### Claude Team and Enterprise

For Claude Team or Enterprise, an Owner or Primary Owner must add Airschool through **Custom → Web** before members can connect.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Owner adds the organization connector">
    Open **Organization settings → Connectors**, choose **Add**, hover over **Custom**, select **Web**, and enter `https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp`. Add the connector to the organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Each member authorizes Airschool">
    Each member opens **Customize → Connectors**, finds Airschool MCP, clicks **Connect**, and authenticates with their own Airschool account in the browser.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Each member enables the tools">
    Select Airschool MCP and the tools needed for the conversation. Organization approval makes the connector available; it does not share an Owner's Airschool authorization with members.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Claude Code setup

Load `AIRSCALE_API_KEY` through an OS or team secret manager or a protected runtime environment before starting Claude Code. Do not type a literal API key into a shell command or shell history.

Create a project-scoped `.mcp.json` at the project root:

```json Project .mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "airscale": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${AIRSCALE_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The `${AIRSCALE_API_KEY}` expression is resolved from the Claude Code process environment. Never replace it with a literal secret in `.mcp.json`; each developer supplies the environment value independently.

From the project root, verify that Claude Code loaded the server:

```bash
claude mcp list
```

Inside Claude Code, run `/mcp` to inspect connection status and the available tools. See the official [Claude Code MCP scope documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp) before choosing a different scope; local and user configurations live in `~/.claude.json`, not in the project file.

## Recommended first prompts

The identities and domains below are synthetic.

> Use `airscale_check_credits` to show my current Airschool credit balance. Do not call another tool.

This is the free connection test. A returned balance confirms tool discovery and authentication to an Airschool workspace without debiting credits, but it does not identify which workspace. Hosted users must verify the OAuth-selected workspace, and Claude Code users must verify which workspace owns the configured credential before paid actions.

> Use Airschool MCP to count people named Taylor Example at `northstar.example`. Do not run a paid search.

> Plan an Airschool search for up to five companies matching `sample-company.test`. Show the proposed Airschool tool, arguments, and maximum cost, then wait for my approval.

For a complete staged sequence, follow the [safe MCP workflow](/mcp/how-to-use-the-airscale-mcp).

## Export behavior

A people or company export performs a fresh paid search from the final filters; it does not package the selected chat rows and may return different rows. Before approval, review the exact filters, fields, format, `max_rows`, additional maximum credits, and cumulative workflow maximum.

An export has one asynchronous lifecycle: start the export once, check its status, then retrieve the file when it is ready. Reuse the same `export_id` and honor the returned `poll_after_seconds`. Do not start a duplicate export while the original job is queued or running.

## Credits and confirmation

The credit check, people count, company filter-value discovery, export status, and export-file retrieval are free. Search and enrichment tools can consume credits; Airsearch costs 2 credits per call. Managed contact enrichment is work-email-only in its current phase.

Paid export starts fail closed until `confirm_credit_spend` is explicitly `true`. Review Claude's proposed tool, arguments, row limit, and maximum cost before confirming. An export can support up to 10,000 rows, but use the smallest limit that serves the task.

## Refreshing tools

If Airschool tools are stale or missing, refresh or reconnect the hosted connector and start a new conversation. In Claude Code, verify the environment and server with `claude mcp list`, then use `/mcp` to inspect the refreshed connection.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Hosted connector controls are unavailable">
    Confirm that the Claude client and account support remote MCP connectors. In Team or Enterprise, ask an Owner or Primary Owner to add Airschool before each member connects their own account.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="OAuth opens but the connection stays pending">
    Complete the Airschool browser sign-in, wait for the authorization confirmation, and return to Claude. Reconnect while signed in to the intended workspace if the state does not update.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Claude Code reports an authentication error">
    Confirm that the environment variable is available to the Claude Code process and that the project configuration uses the `Bearer` scheme. Do not print the value while debugging.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="An export remains queued">
    Poll `airscale_get_export_status` with the same identifier and the returned `poll_after_seconds`. Do not create another paid job.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Security note

Hosted Claude users should authorize only the Airschool workspace they intend to use. Claude Code users should keep the environment value out of version control, prompts, and tool inputs. For either method, review every proposed paid action and remove access when it is no longer needed.

- Read the [Airschool MCP server overview](/mcp/airscale-mcp-server) for authentication and security guidance.

## Airschool MCP Server

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/mcp/airscale-mcp-server.md

Description: Connect Airschool to your AI assistant and prospect without leaving the chat.

Airschool MCP gives compatible AI assistants a concise, typed interface for prospecting through conversation while keeping authentication and paid actions explicit.

## MCP server URL

```text
https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp
```

This remote Streamable HTTP server works with hosted assistants and trusted developer clients. For hosted clients, OAuth is preferred and uses browser sign-in. The Airschool MCP server resolves the authorized workspace credential server-side; the client neither receives nor stores the API key.

Trusted header-capable developer clients must load `AIRSCALE_API_KEY` from a protected runtime environment or secret manager. Never place a literal API key in a prompt or tool argument, source or browser code, or a shell command or shell history.

## Getting started

1. First, choose the setup guide for your assistant.
2. Then connect it to the MCP server URL above.
3. Complete browser OAuth or authenticate from a protected developer runtime.
4. Select and verify the intended workspace.
5. Run `airscale_check_credits` as the free connection check before any paid tool.

The credit check confirms authentication to an Airschool workspace without debiting credits, but it does not identify which workspace. Verify the workspace selected during OAuth—or the workspace that owns a developer credential—before paid actions.

## Setup walkthroughs

- [ChatGPT setup guide](/mcp/connect-airscale-mcp-to-chatgpt)
- [Claude setup guide](/mcp/connect-airscale-mcp-to-claude)
- [Airschool MCP workflow](/mcp/how-to-use-the-airscale-mcp)

These guides contain the client-specific connection steps; this page keeps the shared server contract in one place.

## What you can do

- **People and companies search:** discover prospects with bounded, structured searches.
- **Filter discovery:** inspect available filters and counts before requesting rows.
- **Contact and profile enrichment:** add professional contact details or public person and company profiles.
- **Airsearch:** answer natural-language research questions with structured results.
- **Downloadable exports:** create bounded people, company, or managed contact files and retrieve them when complete.

The [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools) is the schema reference for all 22 typed tools. Managed contact enrichment is a work-email-only flow; it does not add mobile numbers, personal emails, or profile enrichment.

## Export lifecycle

### People and company exports

People and company exports are fresh paid searches, not packages of selected chat rows. A people export uses the final `query`; a company export uses the final `filters`. Results may differ from the sample, and each export creates an additional charge.

Before confirming, review the final scope, fields, format, `max_rows`, additional maximum credits, and cumulative workflow maximum. At up to 0.1 credits per exported row, the requested limit defines the maximum for this fresh search. Set `confirm_credit_spend` only after that review.

### Managed contact enrichment export

A managed contact enrichment export uses a `batch_id`. The batch remains appendable through `airscale_add_contacts_to_enrichment_batch` until the confirmed start. Review the approved contact count, `work_email` as the only enrichment, fields and format, and the maximum calculated as the approved contact count multiplied by up to 2 credits per contact. Review that additional maximum together with the cumulative workflow maximum. After reviewing the contact count and maximum, do not add more contacts.

If the batch may have changed, rerun `airscale_start_contact_enrichment_export` with `confirm_credit_spend` set to false or omitted to obtain the current maximum, then review again. Only after approval should you set it to true. That confirmed start creates the export job and freezes the batch.

### One export lifecycle

Both branches use one asynchronous lifecycle:

1. Run the **confirmed start** once. An unconfirmed managed-contact maximum check does not create a job. Keep the returned `export_id`, and do not start a duplicate export while the job is queued or running.
2. While status is `queued` or `running`, check **status** with the same `export_id` and respect the returned `poll_after_seconds`.
3. When status is `completed` or `failed`, stop polling. Retrieve the **file** with the same `export_id` only after completion.

## How credits work

- Free operations include the credit check, planning, people count or company filter discovery, export status polling, and completed file retrieval.
- Find People and Find Companies each cost 0.1 credit per returned row.
- Airsearch costs 2 credits per call.
- The managed work-email-only contact enrichment phase costs up to 2 credits per contact.
- Paid export starts fail closed until `confirm_credit_spend` is explicitly set after review.

For exact per-tool behavior, use the [MCP tool catalog](/mcp/tools).

## Recommended workflow

1. Run `airscale_check_credits` for a free connection check.
2. Verify the intended workspace before choosing a paid path.

### People and company search/export

1. Use a free count or filter discovery tool to plan the request.
2. Run a bounded sample and inspect the returned shape.
3. Review the workspace, results, and credit implications before continuing.
4. For optional enrichment, request separate approval with its own maximum and updated cumulative spend.
5. Before exporting, perform a renewed export review of the final `query` or `filters`, fields, format, `max_rows`, additional maximum credits, and cumulative workflow maximum.
6. Set `confirm_credit_spend` only after approval, then start once.

### Managed contact enrichment/export

1. Create a batch with `airscale_create_contact_enrichment_batch`.
2. Use `airscale_add_contacts_to_enrichment_batch` while the batch is appendable before the confirmed start.
3. Review the approved contact count, `work_email`, fields and format.
4. Calculate the maximum from the approved contact count multiplied by up to 2 credits per contact, then review the additional maximum and cumulative workflow maximum.
5. After reviewing the contact count and maximum, do not add more contacts.
6. If the batch may have changed, rerun `airscale_start_contact_enrichment_export` with `confirm_credit_spend` set to false or omitted to obtain the current maximum, then review again.
7. Only after approval should you set `confirm_credit_spend` to true. That confirmed start creates the export job and freezes the batch.

### Finish either export

Start once. While status is `queued` or `running`, poll status for the same export job using the same `export_id` and returned `poll_after_seconds`. When status is `completed` or `failed`, stop polling; retrieve the file only after completion. Do not start the export again.

## Security notes

- OAuth keeps workspace credential resolution server-side; the hosted client does not receive or store the Airschool API key.
- Header-capable developer clients should read `AIRSCALE_API_KEY` only from a protected runtime environment or secret manager.
- Never put a literal key in prompts, tool arguments, source control, browser code, shell commands, or shell history.
- Verify the intended workspace before paid actions because a credit balance alone does not identify it.
- Review every paid tool name, scope, and maximum cost before approval.
- If a developer API key is exposed or suspected compromised, rotate it immediately, update the protected secret, and reconnect every trusted client that used it.
- Treat tokenized export URLs and exported files as sensitive. Never place them in prompts or logs, and follow your organization's access, retention, and deletion rules.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="The client cannot authenticate">
    For OAuth, restart browser sign-in and verify the intended workspace. For a header-capable developer client, confirm that its protected runtime can read the configured secret.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="The Airschool tools do not appear">
    Confirm that the server URL is exactly `https://mcp.airscale.io/mcp`, then disconnect and reconnect so the client refreshes all 22 tools.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="A request reports insufficient credits">
    Run `airscale_check_credits`, reduce the paid scope, and review the maximum again. Do not repeatedly submit the same paid request.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="An export is still running">
    Continue polling the same `export_id` at `poll_after_seconds`. Do not create a duplicate while its outcome is unknown.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Airscale CLI

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/cli/overview.md

Description: Search people and companies, enrich work emails from CSV or JSONL, and follow runs from your terminal.

`airscale` brings people search, company search, work-email enrichment, and credit checks to your terminal. Use it interactively or in scripts, with JSON, JSONL, CSV, and table output.

File enrichment saves its progress so you can resume an interrupted run and retrieve the completed file.

## Install

Requires **Node.js 20.3 or newer**.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="npx (no install)">
    ```bash
    npx @airscale/cli --help
    ```

    Replace `airscale` with `npx @airscale/cli` in the examples below.
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="npm (global)">
    ```bash
    npm install --global @airscale/cli
    airscale --help
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Authenticate

Create a workspace API key in [Settings → API key](https://app.airscale.io/dashboard), then save it through the hidden terminal prompt:

```bash
airscale auth set-key
airscale auth status --json
airscale credits --json
```

`auth status` makes a free credit check to verify connectivity. It displays the credential source and a short fingerprint, without printing the key.

For CI, configure `AIRSCALE_API_KEY` through your secret manager. It takes precedence over saved credentials. API keys cannot be passed as command-line arguments.

To remove your saved credential:

```bash
airscale auth logout
```

Logout removes the locally stored key. It does not revoke the key or unset `AIRSCALE_API_KEY`.

## Quick examples

### Search for people

Find up to 20 people for a maximum of 2 credits:

```bash
airscale people search \
  --title CTO --title "VP Engineering" \
  --company-domain example.com --location France \
  --size 20 --max-credits 2 --confirm-credit-spend --json
```

### Export a company search

Follow pages up to 200 companies and save the results as CSV:

```bash
airscale companies search \
  --country France --industry Software \
  --size 50 --all --limit 200 \
  --max-credits 20 --confirm-credit-spend \
  --format csv --output companies.csv
```

Searches cost **0.1 credit per returned result**. Before sending a paid search, the CLI checks the maximum row budget and available credits. An interactive terminal asks for confirmation; scripts require `--confirm-credit-spend`. Add `--max-credits` to enforce a positive-integer credit ceiling.

### Preview and enrich a file

Start with a CSV or JSONL file containing a LinkedIn profile URL, or a first name, last name, and company domain or name. For example:

```csv contacts.csv
first_name,last_name,domain
Jordan,Example,example.com
Taylor,Example,example.org
```

Validate the file and preview the maximum of **2 credits per row** without authentication, network requests, or credit spend:

```bash
airscale enrich file contacts.csv \
  --output contacts-enriched.csv --max-credits 4 --dry-run --json
```

After reviewing the preview, start the work-email enrichment:

```bash
airscale enrich file contacts.csv \
  --output contacts-enriched.csv --max-credits 4 \
  --confirm-credit-spend --resume --json
```

Run the same command again after an interruption. `--resume` reuses the saved batch and run; the input, output path, field, format, and API URL must match. The default state file is `contacts-enriched.csv.airscale-state.json`.

### Follow a run

Use the `exp_…` run ID from your enrichment output or saved state:

```bash
airscale runs status exp_example --json
airscale runs wait exp_example --json
```

These commands are free status reads. To download the completed enrichment file, rerun `enrich file` with `--resume`.

See the [command reference](/cli/commands) for every command, flag, input rule, and pagination behavior.

## Output and exit codes

Interactive results default to a compact table on **stderr**. Pipes and file output default to JSON. Progress and errors also go to stderr; `--quiet` hides progress.

For `credits`, search, and run commands, choose `--json`, `--jsonl`, or `--format json|jsonl|csv|table`. `--output path` writes a file; `--output -` uses the selected format's normal stream. When flags are combined, `--json` takes precedence over `--jsonl`, then `--format`.

Search JSON includes the response envelope and continuation cursor. CSV and JSONL contain the result records. Use JSON when you need pagination metadata.

`enrich file` requires a real output path and supports CSV or JSONL for the completed file. Add `--json` for its separate summary on stdout.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Success. |
| `2` | Invalid command, option, input, state, or file access. |
| `3` | Missing or invalid authentication or configuration. |
| `4` | Credit ceiling, insufficient credits, confirmation, or admission failure. |
| `5` | API or durable-run failure. |
| `130` | Interrupted with Ctrl-C; enrichment state is retained. |

## Configuration

| Setting | Configuration | Precedence or default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API key | `AIRSCALE_API_KEY` or `airscale auth set-key` | Environment variable before saved credentials. |
| API URL | `--base-url` or `AIRSCALE_API_BASE_URL` | Flag, then environment variable, then `https://api.airscale.io/v1`. |
| Credential file directory | `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/airscale`, otherwise `~/.config/airscale`. |

Saved credentials use the optional system keychain when available, under service `airscale` and account `default`. Otherwise they are stored in `config.json` inside the credential directory, with file permissions `0600` and directory permissions `0700`. If the keychain cannot save the key, unlock it and retry.

API URLs must use HTTPS, except for HTTP on loopback addresses such as `http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1`. URLs containing credentials, query parameters, or fragments are rejected.

```bash
airscale --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1 auth status --json
```

---

## Command reference

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/cli/commands.md

Description: Every Airscale CLI command, argument, and flag for authentication, search, file enrichment, credits, and runs.

This reference covers `@airscale/cli` **0.1.0**. Start with [Airscale CLI](/cli/overview) for installation and authentication.

## Global flags and help

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Write JSON to stdout. For `enrich file`, applies to the summary, not the completed file. |
| `--base-url <url>` | Override the API URL and `AIRSCALE_API_BASE_URL`. Default: `https://api.airscale.io/v1`. |
| `--quiet` | Hide progress and informational messages. Errors and result output remain visible. |
| `-V, --version` | Show the CLI version. |
| `-h, --help` | Show help for the current command. |

Use `airscale help [command]` for a top-level command or append `--help` to any nested command. Groups such as `auth`, `people`, `companies`, `enrich`, and `runs` organize the actions below.

```bash
airscale --version
airscale help people
airscale people search --help
airscale enrich file --help
```

### Output flags

These flags are available on `credits`, `people search`, `companies search`, `runs status`, and `runs wait`.

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--output <path>` | Write to a file. `-` selects the normal output stream: stderr for tables, stdout for other formats. |
| `--format <format>` | One of `json`, `jsonl`, `csv`, or `table`. Defaults to a table in an interactive terminal, JSON otherwise or when writing to a file. |
| `--jsonl` | Emit one JSON object per line. Search output contains result records. |

The global `--json` flag wins over `--jsonl`, which wins over `--format`. JSON search output preserves the response envelope; CSV and JSONL omit that envelope. Select the format explicitly when writing a `.csv` or `.jsonl` search file: the filename does not select its format.

### Credit flags

These flags are available on both search commands and `enrich file`.

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--confirm-credit-spend` | Confirm the maximum credit exposure. Required to start fresh paid work in non-interactive mode; otherwise the CLI asks in the terminal. |
| `--max-credits <credits>` | Positive integer ceiling for the maximum exposure. Reject the command if the estimate exceeds it. Does not replace spend confirmation. |

Credit checks are free. Search costs 0.1 credit per returned result. File enrichment previews a maximum of 2 credits per row. These commands check available credits before starting fresh paid work.

## Authentication

### `airscale auth set-key`

Store an API key through a hidden terminal prompt. Takes no arguments or command-specific flags. The prompt requires an interactive terminal; configure `AIRSCALE_API_KEY` through your CI secret manager for scripts.

```bash
airscale auth set-key
```

The optional system keychain is used when available, otherwise the CLI writes a restricted local credential file. `AIRSCALE_API_KEY` overrides the stored key. There is no API-key command-line flag.

### `airscale auth status`

Check configured authentication and API connectivity with a free credits request. Takes no arguments or command-specific flags; use global `--json` for machine-readable status.

```bash
airscale auth status --json
```

A successful status includes `configured`, `connected`, `source`, `fingerprint`, and `base_url`. Missing credentials produce `configured: false`, `connected: false`, and `source: "none"`, then exit `3`. Invalid credentials also exit `3`. The full API key is never displayed.

### `airscale auth logout`

Remove locally saved credentials. Takes no arguments or command-specific flags.

```bash
airscale auth logout
```

This does not revoke the API key. If `AIRSCALE_API_KEY` is set, it remains active until removed from the environment.

## Credits

### `airscale credits`

Show the authenticated workspace's remaining credits. This request is free. Supports all [output flags](#output-flags).

```bash
airscale credits --json
airscale credits --format csv --output credits.csv
```

## Search

### Shared search flags

Both searches support the [output flags](#output-flags), [credit flags](#credit-flags), and these pagination and request options:

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--request <path>` | Read an advanced public API request from a JSON file. Cannot be combined with convenience filters. |
| `--size <size>` | Page size, from `1` to `100`. Defaults to `100` for people and `50` for companies; a company cursor carries its own page size. |
| `--cursor <cursor>` | Continue a previous search. Overrides the request file's cursor. |
| `--all` | Follow continuation cursors until exhausted or the row limit is reached. |
| `--limit <rows>` | Maximum returned rows, from `1` to `10000`. With `--all`, defaults to `10000`. Without `--all`, limits a single page. |

`--size` also overrides a request file's size. Without `--all`, the maximum exposure is the smaller of the page size and `--limit`. With `--all`, it is `--limit` (or 10,000) multiplied by 0.1 credits.

People page sizes shrink to the remaining row budget. Company cursors require a full page: the CLI stops before another page would exceed `--limit` and preserves its continuation cursor. A supplied company cursor must have a recognizable page size that fits the approved request. To continue later, keep the filters unchanged and pass the returned `next_cursor`.

Paid search requests are not automatically retried. If a response is lost or ambiguous, inspect API request logs before repeating the search.

### `airscale people search`

Search for people with common filters or an advanced [Find People request](/api-reference/find-people).

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--title <value>` | Job title. Repeat to include multiple titles. |
| `--company-domain <domain>` | Company domain. Repeat to include multiple domains. |
| `--location <value>` | Location. Repeat to include multiple locations. |

Each convenience filter maps to an `include` list in the API query. Also supports every [shared search flag](#shared-search-flags).

```bash
airscale people search \
  --title CTO --title "VP Engineering" \
  --company-domain example.com --location France \
  --size 20 --max-credits 2 --confirm-credit-spend --json
```

For advanced filters, save a JSON object with the public request schema:

```json people-query.json
{
  "query": {
    "JobTitle": { "include": ["CTO"], "exclude": ["Assistant"] },
    "currentCompany.headcount": { ">=": 20, "<=": 200 }
  },
  "size": 25
}
```

```bash
airscale people search --request people-query.json \
  --max-credits 3 --confirm-credit-spend --jsonl --output people.jsonl
```

This example's maximum exposure is 2.5 credits, within the integer ceiling of 3. Unknown top-level request keys and filter names are rejected before the search.

### `airscale companies search`

Search for companies with common filters or an advanced [Find Companies request](/api-reference/find-companies). At least one real filter is required.

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--country <value>` | Country. Repeat to include multiple countries. |
| `--industry <value>` | Industry. Repeat to include multiple industries. |

Also supports every [shared search flag](#shared-search-flags).

```bash
airscale companies search \
  --country France --country Germany --industry Software \
  --size 50 --all --limit 200 \
  --max-credits 20 --confirm-credit-spend \
  --format csv --output companies.csv
```

Advanced requests use the public `filters` object. See [company filter values](/api-reference/find-companies/filter-values) for supported values.

```json company-query.json
{
  "filters": {
    "country": ["France"],
    "industry": ["Software"]
  },
  "size": 20
}
```

```bash
airscale companies search --request company-query.json \
  --max-credits 2 --confirm-credit-spend --json
```

## File enrichment

### `airscale enrich file <input>`

Enrich a CSV or JSONL file with professional work emails. The CLI uploads the validated rows, starts one durable run, waits for completion, and writes the verified result file.

| Argument or flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<input>` | A `.csv` or `.jsonl` path, or `-` to read stdin and detect the format. Maximum 10,000 records. |
| `--output <path>` | Required completed output file. Must differ from the input and cannot be `-`. |
| `--field <field>` | Defaults to `work_email`, the only supported field. |
| `--format <format>` | Completed file format: `csv` or `jsonl`. Defaults to JSONL for a `.jsonl` output filename, CSV otherwise. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate every row and preview maximum exposure locally, without credentials, HTTP requests, or credit spend. |
| `--resume` | Continue the saved run with the same input, output, field, format, and API URL. With no saved state, prepares a fresh run. |
| `--state-file <path>` | Override the default `<output>.airscale-state.json`. Must differ from the input and output paths. |

Also supports the [credit flags](#credit-flags). Use global `--json` for the summary; it does not change the completed file format. `--jsonl` is not an enrichment flag.

#### Input columns

Each row needs either:

- `linkedin_profile_url`; or
- `first_name` and `last_name`, with `domain` or `company_name`.

```csv contacts.csv
first_name,last_name,domain
Jordan,Example,example.com
Taylor,Example,example.org
```

CSV headers are trimmed, lowercased, and spaces or hyphens become underscores for identity matching. Original columns and values remain in the output. CSV quoting, embedded newlines, UTF-8 BOMs, and Unicode are supported. JSONL records must be objects.

Invalid identities, duplicate normalized CSV headers, malformed CSV, and duplicate `custom_id` values stop the command before HTTP. Row-level identity and JSONL validation errors are reported together. Missing IDs are assigned in row order as `airscale-row-1`, `airscale-row-2`, and so on.

#### Preview and start

```bash
airscale enrich file contacts.csv \
  --field work_email --output contacts-enriched.csv \
  --max-credits 4 --dry-run --json
```

After reviewing the preview:

```bash
airscale enrich file contacts.csv \
  --field work_email --output contacts-enriched.csv \
  --max-credits 4 --confirm-credit-spend --resume --json
```

For stdin and JSONL output:

```bash
cat contacts.csv | airscale enrich file - \
  --output contacts-enriched.jsonl --format jsonl \
  --max-credits 4 --confirm-credit-spend --resume --json
```

To resume stdin, supply the exact same input bytes again.

#### Output and recovery

Results add `custom_id`, `work_email`, `email_status`, and `status` when returned. Existing input fields are preserved; collisions receive an `airscale_` prefix and, if needed, `_2`, `_3`, and so on. An input `work_email` column therefore stays intact while its result is written to `airscale_work_email`.

The CLI verifies completed metadata, format, row count, and custom-ID order before committing the output atomically. An existing output with different content is preserved.

Keep the state file until the run is fully reconciled. It records the input hash, output path, field, format, API URL, batch ID, run ID, and idempotency key, without API credentials. `--resume` refuses mismatched inputs and continues the same batch and run after a lost upload or start response. It never creates a replacement batch automatically.

Ctrl-C aborts local requests and polling, removes temporary downloads, retains state, and exits `130`. It does not cancel server work. Resume with the original command to retrieve the result. An unknown start handoff is reported for inspection and is not automatically replayed.

Locks protect both the output and state paths. If a crash leaves a reported `.airscale-lock` file, inspect its PID and remove the lock only after that process has stopped, then resume. A completed matching output can be resumed safely.

## Runs

Run IDs start with `exp_`. Both commands perform free reads and support all [output flags](#output-flags).

### `airscale runs status <id>`

Fetch the current status of a durable enrichment run once. `<id>` is required; there are no other command-specific flags.

```bash
airscale runs status exp_example --json
```

The command reports a failed run as status data. Use `runs wait` if a failed run should produce a failing exit code.

### `airscale runs wait <id>`

Poll until the run completes or fails. `<id>` is required; there are no other command-specific flags. A failed run exits `5`.

```bash
airscale runs wait exp_example --json
airscale runs wait exp_example --quiet --output run.json
```

Polling follows the server's recommended interval, bounded to 2–60 seconds. Transient status-read failures use bounded retries; `429` respects `Retry-After`, including waits longer than 60 seconds. Ctrl-C stops local waiting and exits `130`.

Run commands return status metadata. To retrieve the completed enrichment file, run `enrich file` again with `--resume` and the original input and output paths.

## Quick beginner guide

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/usecases/quick-beginner-guide.md

Description: This quick beginner tutorial shows you how to navigate the Airschool platform and start using its key features

<iframe
  className="w-full aspect-video rounded-xl"
  src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/6EtRvjMBgfs?iv_load_policy=3&amp;rel=0&amp;modestbranding=1&amp;playsinline=1&amp;autoplay=0"
  title="Quick beginner guide video walkthrough"
  allow="accelerometer; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture"
  allowFullScreen
></iframe>

In this video, we walk through the fundamentals of Airschool, from building targeted lead lists to enriching them with high-quality data in real time.

## Core functionalities

Airschool is built around two main use cases:

- Building lead lists
- Enriching contacts

Unlike traditional tools, it is not a database, instead, it pulls real-time data from multiple sources such as LinkedIn, Sales Navigator, Apollo, and Google Maps.

## Building lists

The process starts with the Leads Finder module. By applying filters on both people and companies, you can define your targeting and preview results in real time.

Once you're satisfied, you can load up to 10,000 contacts into a table. This table already includes key information such as:

- Names
- Job titles
- Location
- Company details
- Domain
- LinkedIn profile

## Data enrichment

From there, you can enrich your data directly within the platform. You simply select the rows and choose what type of enrichment you want to run:

- Emails
- Phone numbers
- People data
- Company data
- etc.

Airschool uses a waterfall enrichment logic for emails and phones, meaning multiple providers are tested automatically to maximize results. Importantly, no credits are used when no data is found.

## Built-in AI feature

Airschool also includes a built-in AI feature that allows you to go further with your data. You can write prompts, select different LLMs, and optionally connect your own API key.

Depending on your setup:

- Without web access → analyze or summarize existing data
- With web access → retrieve or scrape external information

## Export and integrations

Once your data is ready, you can easily export it as a CSV or send it directly to your existing tools, including CRMs (Hubspot, Salesforce) and outbound platforms (Lemlist, Instantly, SmartLead).

## Workspace & plans

Airschool provides a collaborative workspace where you can manage your profile, invite team members for free, and access billing.

Several plans are available, all without commitment:

- Starter (49\$)
- Pro (99\$)
- Growth (189\$ to 1049\$)
- Scale (for higher volumes, custom plans can also be set up)

## API & automation

You can generate an API key and connect Airschool to tools like Clay. This allows you to automate enrichment workflows and significantly reduce costs.

If you have any questions, feel free to reach out, the Airschool team is always happy to help.

## The basics of AI

Source: https://airscale.mintlify.app/usecases/the-basics-of-ai.md

Description: Run AI on Airschool with the best LLMs using custom prompts

## 1. Why use the AI enrichment with Airschool ?

Manual contact enrichment or cleaning is slow, and impossible to scale. Airschool's AI enrichment module automates the entire process, directly from your lead lists. For example:

- Infer job seniority and ICP fit
- Generate personalized icebreakers
- Summarize company positioning
- Detect buying intent signals

All of it produced in seconds, turning raw contact data into actionable sales intelligence, without any manual work.

To use AI, just click on the blue **"Use AI"** button in the top right corner of your table.

<video className="w-full rounded-xl" src="/videos/usecases/Rr8MizcUxj0UhJlhJQGtlXHits.mp4" autoPlay muted loop playsInline controls aria-label="The basics of AI video walkthrough" />

## 2. Classic LLMs vs Airsearch

The second step of your enrichment panel (after selecting the rows to use AI on) is the "Web access?" mode.

- **No web access:** Best to edit, format, or clean your data. Use this mode when your prompt only needs data already existing in your table and doesn’t need to browse the web to provide the expected output

- **Web access:** Use this mode if you want to find data on the web and want AI to have web browsing capabilities. Useful to research data online about a company or a prospect by visiting the web / website pages (*this mode will select Airsearch 1.0 as the default LLM to use).* Check our [Using Airsearch](/usecases/using-airsearch) guide for more information

Click on the toggle **"No web access / Web access"** to choose either mode.

<video className="w-full rounded-xl" src="/videos/usecases/NDRZsyscdycMIRLpXvfc5JflFM.mp4" autoPlay muted loop playsInline controls aria-label="The basics of AI video walkthrough" />

## 3. How to prompt

A good AI enrichment prompt always includes three elements:

### Good inputs

Each input variable (e.g. First name, Job title …) must be manually linked to its corresponding column in your table. Click on the variable in your prompt and select the matching column: it turns blue once correctly connected.

![The basics of AI — Good inputs](/images/usecases/eU6f1aB32XWmlbwdY3Ifj8dzYI.gif)

### Context

Start by telling the AI who it is and what it's doing. A prompt that opens with *"You are a B2B market research analyst. Your goal is to…"* will produce sharper, more relevant results than one that dives straight into the task. From there, break down the instructions into explicit steps: what data to look at first, what to infer from it, what to prioritize, and what to ignore. The more structured your instructions, the more consistent and reliable the output across your entire lead list.

<video className="w-full rounded-xl" src="/videos/usecases/Httm9dqhOsf4YCmpkFgrmtI5EdY.mp4" autoPlay muted loop playsInline controls aria-label="The basics of AI video walkthrough" />

### Output indication

Specify the exact format expected. The AI will fill whatever shape you give it. If you need a one-liner for a CRM field, say so. If you need a three-bullet summary, define each bullet. Specifying the format, tone, length, and any constraints (no filler phrases, always use second person, flag if data is missing) ensures the output is immediately usable, with no manual cleanup required.

*When using Airsearch, you can define your outputs with even more precision, check our* [*Using Airsearch*](/usecases/using-airsearch) *guide for more information*

<video className="w-full rounded-xl" src="/videos/usecases/Shf9tlX4URyeUPl7K0XHH72Xz0E.mp4" autoPlay muted loop playsInline controls aria-label="The basics of AI video walkthrough" />

## 4. Save & import templates

Once you've built a prompt that works, you don't want to rewrite it from scratch every time. Airschool lets you save any AI enrichment prompt as a reusable template, so your best configurations are always one click away.

Saved templates can then be imported directly into any workflow or enrichment column, whether you're setting up a new campaign, onboarding a new lead list, or simply duplicating a process that's already proven its value. No copy-pasting, no risk of losing a prompt that took time to calibrate.

This is especially useful for teams: instead of each member building their own version of the same prompt, you define a shared standard once, save it, and everyone works from the same reliable baseline.

### How to save a new template:

![The basics of AI — How to save a new template:](/images/usecases/D05iTJ5SmQUfgNmwCCxvQP1B3ig.gif)

### How to import a template:

![The basics of AI — How to import a template:](/images/usecases/mqr19fbeSJslAcNI1WEh8yipPI.gif)

**Note:** When importing a template, make sure to rewrite your inputs as they won't be automatically connected to the columns in your table.

## 5. Connect your own LLM

You can connect your own API key by going in the platform **Settings** and then, in the **Integrations** section.

Paste your key. Once that's connected, the key next to the LLM turns green (when selecting your LLM in **"Use AI"**)

<video className="w-full rounded-xl" src="/videos/usecases/NCvu1jSULLzmb0X8v8vbRB3er50.mp4" autoPlay muted loop playsInline controls aria-label="The basics of AI video walkthrough" />

## 6. Results

### Classic LLM results

If you've chosen not to grant web access to your search, then only one column will appear at the end of your table: **"AI"**

If you click on the expand icon, you will be able to see the full AI response.

![The basics of AI — Classic LLM results](/images/usecases/zbxyF6OSaU3UiiAKDIScAPXgJM.gif)

### Airsearch results

Two columns usually appear at the end of your table when the workflow has run:

- Left column - **"Search completed ✅"**, & **"Click to expand"** which reveals the AI reasoning and details of the search

  Click on **"Click to expand"** to access information such as the details of the reasoning, the sources, the certainty of the search results etc.

  **Note :** You can add any of these fields as new columns if you click on **"Add as a column +"**, including the one you might have created with the **"Define outputs"** section

- Right column - the direct answer to your prompt
